# FDGA046

> DO use auto-implemented properties when the implementation is unlikely to change.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.6 Other.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: IDE0032
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

With C# 14 and later, IDE0032 also reports a property whose accessors have logic around one backing field, such as validation in the setter or a call after the assignment, and its fix turns it into a property that uses the field keyword (probe with SDK 10.0.402 and the default language version of net10.0); that is not an auto-implemented property.

## Options

```ini
dotnet_style_prefer_auto_properties = true
```

## From the book

```csharp
internal partial class SomeCache
{
    internal long HitCount { get; private set; }
    internal long MissCount { get; private set; }
}
```
